text: Continuous integration, or CI, is a software development practice that helps teams work faster and with fewer mistakes. When developers add new code to a shared project, automated builds start immediately. These builds check that the code works correctly and combine it with the rest of the project. During the build, the system also runs tests to make sure nothing is broken. This way, teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organize all these steps into a clear process: build, test, and report results. By using CI, developers can find bugs quickly, save time, and deliver better software to users.
